documents.title: Weakness and stretch marks
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello, I wanted you to know my legs have gotten so weak I have to pull myself up the stairs with the railing and I need my arms to get out of a chair. I've gained weight this year even though I'm eating less and I have these purple stretch marks on my belly. I bruise if I bump anything. I have my endocrinology follow-up on February 14. Should I keep that or come see you first? Beverly

documents.title: RE: Weakness and stretch marks
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me. Keep the endocrinology appointment - those are exactly the right people for this, and I'll send them a note ahead of time. If you fall, get short of breath, or the weakness suddenly gets worse, call us that day. Let's book a visit with me in early March to go over what they find.

events.reason: Fatigue, proximal weakness, weight gain, abdominal striae

conditions.label: Long term (current) use of systemic steroids
conditions.note: glucocorticoid excess features from long-term prednisone

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit: 02/14/2022

Seen one year after her first visit here for secondary hyperparathyroidism (CKD 3b) and osteoporosis, with RA.

Interval history: Fatigue keeps progressing. Proximal weakness over the past year - pulls up the stairs by the rail, uses her arms to rise from a chair, has trouble holding her arms up to comb her hair. Weight up despite eating less. Skin tears and bruises easily; new reddish-purple stretch marks across the abdomen. Two admissions in 2021 for COPD flares requiring intubation, each treated with high-dose IV steroids on top of her daily prednisone. Appetite and sleep unchanged. No fevers, chest pain or palpitations.

Medications: metformin, amlodipine, fluticasone-salmeterol, albuterol, methotrexate, and prednisone 10 mg daily (RA and COPD); also glyburide, lisinopril, HCTZ, omeprazole, aspirin, alendronate, calcium, vitamin D3.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 164/92, pulse 86. BMI 31. Round, full face. Fullness above both clavicles and a prominent dorsocervical fat pad. Thin arms and legs with proximal muscle wasting. Wide violaceous striae across the abdomen. Scattered ecchymoses on forearms.

Assessment: Clinical glucocorticoid excess from long-term exogenous prednisone (cumulative dose substantial, plus two hospital steroid courses). Steroid myopathy explains the proximal weakness, and steroids are worsening her glucose control, blood pressure and bone loss. No evidence of an endogenous source is needed to explain this; biochemical testing for endogenous cortisol excess is not indicated while she takes prednisone.

Recommendations: The prednisone dose is the central issue. Would ask rheumatology to look at steroid-sparing options for her RA; I recognize her lung disease complicates any taper. Do not stop prednisone abruptly - adrenal suppression is expected. Continue alendronate, calcium and D. Return in one year.

Endocrinology clinic

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Reviewed endo letter of 2/14 with her: weakness, weight gain, striae and bruising are from years of prednisone; BP was 164/92 there.

Today BP improved from that reading but above goal (see vitals); she was rushing in. Home cuff readings she brought: 130s-140s/80s.

She is torn about prednisone. She understands it is hurting her muscles and bones, but she is frightened of another intubation and her rheumatologist and lung history make her want to leave it alone for now. I'll forward the endo letter to rheumatology with a note asking them to weigh in at her next visit. No change today. Strict instruction not to stop it on her own.

T2DM: A1c drawn; expect higher with the steroids. Again offered adding a second-line agent; she wants to wait for the A1c.
HTN: continue current three drugs; recheck at next visit with home log.
Fall risk: proximal weakness - discussed rails, night lights, rising slowly.

RTC 3 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 3-month f/u. Home BP log 128-138/76-84, nice. March A1c 9.3 - she saw it on the portal and has cut out juice. Weakness unchanged, not worse. No falls. No COPD flares since November. Prednisone unchanged.

O: BP as charted, at goal today. Lungs distant, no wheeze. Bruises on forearms. No edema.

A: HTN controlled. T2DM uncontrolled, steroid effect. CKD 3b stable. Glucocorticoid excess - awaiting rheum.
P: MTX labs. Screening mammogram this month. AWV end of August with A1c and urine albumin.

reports.text: Screening bilateral mammography with tomosynthesis. Comparison 6/2020 and 5/2018. Breasts are heterogeneously fatty with scattered fibroglandular tissue. No suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion in either breast.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, subsequent. Accompanied by husband for the first part.

Updates: endocrinology 2/2022 - glucocorticoid excess from prednisone, steroid-sparing options suggested; rheum to address in November. No hospitalizations in 2022 so far. Mammogram negative in June.

Function: independent but slow; uses the rail. No falls. Driving locally. Cognition grossly intact, recall 3/3. PHQ-2 negative.
Advance care planning: reviewed proxy; she does not want prolonged life support if she could not recover to talking and being at home, and would accept another short intubation for a reversible flare. Husband present and agrees.

Exam: vitals as charted. Round face, supraclavicular fullness, abdominal striae fading in color. Lungs distant. Feet intact, sensation normal, pulses present.

Plan: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, UACR, PTH/phos for nephrology. Flu and the updated COVID booster at a nurse visit in late September. RTC December.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Here for seasonal vaccines. High-dose influenza (L arm) and Pfizer bivalent booster (R arm) given, lot numbers in record. Prior doses tolerated. Sat 15 min, fine on departure.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Nephrology annual follow-up, 10/18/2022.

CKD 3b, diabetic and hypertensive, with albuminuria (UACR 240 in August), secondary HPT and anemia of CKD. Creatinine stable in the 1.6 range. Hemoglobin around 11. PTH 170s-180s, calcium and phosphorus normal. Steroid-related glucose elevation noted by endocrinology.

Plan: no changes. Continue vitamin D3. Labs every 6 months through PCP. Return 1 year.

Outside Nephrology Group

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body: RA follow-up 11/15/2022. Joints quiet. Endocrinology letter and PCP note reviewed regarding glucocorticoid excess. Discussed reducing prednisone; patient prefers to keep the current dose after two intubations last year and does not want to risk a lung flare this winter. Will readdress next year. Continue methotrexate 15 mg weekly and prednisone 10 mg daily. Monitoring labs acceptable. Return 12 months.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not arrive for 10:00. Called - she had the date written as next week. Rebooked 12/20 at 9:30. No issues.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated retinal exam 12/6/2022. Acuity 20/30 OD, 20/25 OS with correction; mild cataract progression OD, not visually significant yet. IOP within normal limits. No diabetic retinopathy either eye. No macular edema. Return 12 months.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from 12/6.

Rheum kept prednisone at 10 mg at her request; noted. She is steady: no flares, weakness about the same, weight steady. BP at goal on home log. Feet fine.

Assessment unchanged. A1c, BMP, CBC, LFTs today. RTC spring.
